- **M5** (2026-09-22T17:41:52.812Z) — Version bumps: the version string appears SIX times per file, not once. packages/engine/package.json carries `version` plus five sofar-core optional deps (sofar-core-darwin-arm64, -darwin-x64, -linux-x64, -linux-arm64, -win32-x64) pinned to the same string, and package-lock.json repeats all six. Setting only `version` ships a package whose five core-binary pins resolve the PREVIOUS release — a stale binary on whichever platform nobody tests locally (win32-x64, or a linux arch). So bump by replacing the version string GLOBALLY in both files, and self-check before committing: the result parses as JSON, ZERO occurrences of the old string remain anywhere, the engine version equals the new one, and exactly five sofar-core deps are pinned to it — a count, never an eyeball. (3) packaging/npm/sofar-core-*/package.json — the five platform packages each carry their OWN `version`, and packaging.test.ts asserts each equals the engine manifest's, so missing them fails the suite. Also learned: the five sofar-core-<platform> packages have NEVER been published (npm view → 404 at any version), so an install resolves none of them and install.mjs keeps the JavaScript shim by design — "a missing binary is no core, never a broken install". Pinning them at a new version is therefore safe, and publishing the native core is a separate decision.
And: a release branch in a git worktree must NOT share node_modules with the main checkout by symlink. npm's workspace links inside it point at the MAIN tree, so `require('sofar.sh/package.json')` returns main's version and the packaging test fails with the old string. Give the worktree its own node_modules whose `sofar.sh` and `@sofar/schema` links point INTO the worktree.
- **M7** (2026-09-22T22:34:50.139Z) — A vitest file that fails to LOAD is reported as "not run", never as a failure, so a suite can say PASSED while covering less than it claims — compare test COUNTS, not the word "passed", whenever the environment differs from the one the baseline ran in. Caught staging 0.34.0-rc.1: the release branch reported 3008 passed / 16 skipped against an independent verification of the main it merged at 3011 / 16. The missing three were packages/schema/test/rust-codegen.test.ts, whose top-level import of tools/schema-codegen/emit.mjs needs the devDependency ts-json-schema-generator; the file's own `it.skipIf(cargo missing)` cannot protect an import that never resolved. The cause was a worktree symlinking the main checkout's node_modules (see M6) where that dep is not installed. Fix: give a release worktree its own `npm ci`, then re-run and confirm the count matches or exceeds the base's. A release gated on a suite that quietly skipped a file is not gated.
- **M8** (2026-09-22T22:36:09.216Z) — Release tags: an UNPUSHED tag may be deleted and re-cut — nobody has seen it, so that is editing a draft, and shipping notes known to be wrong is the real damage. The moment a tag is PUSHED it becomes something others have seen, and any correction after that is a NEW tag, never a move: no `git tag -f`, no delete-and-repush. The rule is not "never move a tag", it is "never rewrite what someone else has seen". A corrective tag name like v0.34.0-rc.1a is the wrong answer BEFORE a push (it permanently advertises a mistake that never left the worktree) and the only answer after one. Set staging 0.34.0-rc.1 (drive-visibility 5.2), where the first tag's notes carried a test count that a re-run corrected.
- **M9** (2026-09-23T06:47:27.563Z) — D18 read-path numbers have a RESOLUTION FLOOR that depends on n: at n=25 the same comparison swung ±4.4% between two runs an hour apart, while at n=50 the widest of eight measurements was 1.2% (bench-refresh, sofar-c3, 2026-09-23). So: run a RELEASE gate at n=50, not the default 25; and never quote a signed sub-5% delta from an n=25 run as if it were a measurement — "within budget at n=50, no measurable regression" is both honest and harder to pull apart than a precise-looking number that is indistinguishable from zero. Every per-task D18 figure recorded for drive-visibility 3.2 (+0.6%), 3.3 (+0.9%) and 3.6 (−1.4%) was taken at n=25 and should be read as "no regression detected", not as a measured change. Measurement precondition (bench-refresh M16): AC power AND AppleClamshellState = No, because on battery this machine takes Maintenance Sleeps — two observed on 2026-09-23, 10:50:37 IST for 908 s and 11:06:01 IST for 3 s, both "Using Batt" — and a sleep mid-measure is a timed-out run, not a slow one.
- **M10** (2026-09-23T08:21:23.013Z) — A D18 read-path gate MUST pass `--session <registered id>` (rust-core M20, confirmed here 2026-09-23). bench/read-paths.mjs defaults to session `bench-read-paths`, which is not registered in the fixture's record, so the UserPromptSubmit handler returns at "not ours to nudge" before any per-session work — lessons and their BM25 ranking, told, file conflicts, peers, drift — and the figure measures an early return rather than the path. Proved directly: the same build, same fixture, the unregistered id printed NOTHING while a registered id printed a matched lesson line plus the engine-changed and git lines. The effect is large, not marginal: this rc's gate read sub-1% on all four paths unregistered and +5.1%/+5.3% on session-start and user-prompt registered, over two runs. The check that makes it real is that the hook PRINTS something — a lesson line, or a fresh .sofar/.index/told/<session>.json in the candidate clone. Pick an id that appears in a committed session_started of the fixture's record, since the bench measures the COMMITTED record.
- **M11** (2026-09-23T08:47:23.762Z) — A release staged on a BRANCH cannot be published from a checkout sitting on MAIN, and the failure looks exactly like success. npm discards semver BUILD METADATA, so `npm publish -w sofar.sh --tag next` run from ~/IO/sofar on main — whose package.json reads 0.33.0-rc.2+trunk — silently enqueued plain 0.33.0-rc.2: main's tree, gated by nobody, matching no tag, its five sofar-core pins still naming a version that does not exist. It passed validation and TOOK THE `next` TAG. Happened 2026-09-23 publishing drive-visibility's rc. The one-line check before any publish: `node -p "require('./packages/engine/package.json').version"` in the CWD must equal the version you intend to ship — the staged release lives in its own worktree, so publish from THERE. Recovery, if it happens again: publish the correct artifact so the dist-tag moves to the gated one, then DEPRECATE the accidental version with a message naming its replacement (`npm deprecate sofar.sh@<bad> "published in error from main; use <good>"`) rather than unpublishing — same signal to anyone who finds it, no irreversibility, and unpublish has a 72-hour window and breaks anyone who already resolved it.
